newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Main Tunisian opposition party has new leaders.
newsitem.headline: Main Tunisian opposition party has new leaders.

text.p: Tunisia's main opposition party, the Democrat Socialists Movement (MDS), has changed its leadership, its new secretary general said on Monday.
MDS Secretary-General Ismail Boulahia told a news conference that a congress of some 200 party delegates elected on Sunday a new 11-member politburo.

"The party's line will not change. What is new is that we will put more emphasis on consensual democracy and on the protection of the environment. We support President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali's programme for change and hope all Tunisians support him," Boulahia said.
Boulahia, a publisher and parliament member, was one of two members of the new leadership members who had served on the former politburo.
He said that his group had obtained government recognition before the meeting was held, and the financial support authorities normally give to Tunisia's political parties.

A group led by lawyer Mohammad Khalfallah and including six of the nine members of the outgoing politburo had said in a statement that it was still the legal leader of the party and it would not attend the "illegitimate" congress.
Boulahia said: "We are the sole legitimate leadership, and we will sue in justice the other group whenever they talk in the name of MDS."
The congress was not open to the press.

Boulahia succeeds former party leader Mohammad Moada, who was sentenced in 1996 to 11 years in jail on charges of having secret contacts with Libyan agents and receiving money from Tripoli. He was freed last December but banned from political activity.

MDS was founded in 1978 by a group led by Ahmed Mestiri, who withdrew from politics in 1992. Moada, an Arab nationalist, succeeded him as head of the movement, ousting liberals led by MDS secretary general Mustapha Ben Jaafar in 1993.
